_note: Markdown does not linkify fenced content, so neither do we. This only became consequential with SPEC 10, which makes code in the body the NORMAL case for an Attested Computation: R's `[[ ]]` indexing is literally the wikilink syntax, so a `runtime: r` computation emitted three phantom wikilinks from one function. Phantom BROKEN references are noise; the hazard is a reference in code that happens to match a concept, which becomes a silently false graph edge. Fenced blocks only -- indented blocks are ordinary nested-list continuation, and inline spans are how authors emphasise a real reference (masking them would have dropped 8 resolving edges in a 219-concept wiki).
